enumeration_note: One order-block strategy taught. The three 'entry models' (wick / body / midpoint buy-limit placement) share the identical validation skeleton and stop-loss logic, differing only in entry level and R:R â€” grouped as compatible variants per Rule 3. The bearish/short order block is mentioned only as symmetric definitional context with no runnable entry mechanics, so it stays an unpromoted mention. Take-profit is gestural (risk-to-reward framing only, no explicit level).

coaching_notes: Choosing the right entry model depends on market conditions, the quality of the order block, and your personal risk tolerance
The stronger and cleaner the order block, the more aggressive the entry model you can justify
In weaker or more volatile environments, conservative entries offer greater protection and consistency
Order blocks only work when they align with structure, liquidity, imbalance, and mitigation logic
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: bullish market structure confirmed by a break of structure (price breaking above previous major high) before the order block setup applies
Order block definition: the last bearish candle before a strong bullish displacement that breaks structure
Validation 1 â€” liquidity sweep: final bearish candle breaks the previous candle's low then immediately reverses upward
Validation 2 â€” imbalance/FVG must form above the reversal (non-overlapping candles)
Validation 2 exception: if no imbalance forms above the sweep candle, extend the order block boundary to include the next candle where imbalance is present
Validation 3 â€” unmitigated: price has not returned into the zone; a wick dropping into the zone during formation mitigates and INVALIDATES the order block
Entry model 1 (aggressive): buy limit at upper wick of the order block candle
Entry model 2 (conservative): buy limit at upper level of the candle body
Entry model 3 (optimal): buy limit at midpoint of the order block zone
Stop loss: just below the lower wick of the order block candle, adjusted by the spread
Change of character (break of an internal low) during the retracement into the order block used as the entry trigger
strategies.entry_summary: Identify a valid bullish order block (the last bearish candle before a strong bullish displacement that breaks structure), validated by three criteria: (1) a liquidity sweep where the final bearish candle takes out the prior candle's low then reverses up, (2) an imbalance / fair value gap above the reversal (if no imbalance forms above the sweep candle, extend the order block boundary to include the next candle where imbalance is visible), and (3) the zone remaining unmitigated (price has not returned into it â€” a wick that drops into the zone during formation invalidates it). Enter via a buy limit order placed inside the order block zone; in the live example, a change of character (break of an internal low) during the retracement into the zone acts as the entry trigger.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss placed just below the lower wick of the order block candle, adjusted by the spread. Targets are framed only in terms of risk-to-reward profile â€” no explicit take-profit level is taught.
